title: GLP-1 Drugs: The Molecules Reshaping Medicine

slides.heading: GLP-1 Drugs: The Molecules Reshaping Medicine
slides.body: What started as a diabetes treatment is turning out to be one of the most transformative drug classes in modern history

slides.heading: What Are GLP-1 Drugs?
slides.body: GLP-1 (glucagon-like peptide-1) is a hormone naturally released after eating. Drugs like semaglutide (Ozempic, Wegovy) and tirzepatide mimic this hormone, signaling the brain to feel full, slowing digestion, and regulating blood sugar.

slides.heading: The Weight Loss Breakthrough
slides.body: Clinical trials showed 15–22% body weight loss — far exceeding anything previously possible with medication. Unlike older diet drugs, GLP-1s work on the brain's reward system, reducing cravings rather than just suppressing appetite mechanically.

slides.heading: Heart & Cardiovascular Benefits
slides.body: The SELECT trial found semaglutide reduced major cardiovascular events (heart attack, stroke) by 20% — even in people without diabetes. Cardiologists are now prescribing these drugs specifically for heart protection, not just weight.

slides.heading: Kidney Disease Protection
slides.body: A 2024 landmark trial showed semaglutide cut the risk of kidney failure and dialysis by 24% in patients with chronic kidney disease. This opened a massive new front beyond metabolic health, potentially sparing millions from dialysis.

slides.heading: Fighting Addiction
slides.body: Early trials show GLP-1 drugs reduce cravings for alcohol, nicotine, and opioids — possibly because they quiet the brain's dopamine-driven reward circuits. Researchers are exploring them as treatments for addiction disorders.

slides.heading: Alzheimer's Connection
slides.body: Studies suggest GLP-1 drugs reduce neuroinflammation and may slow cognitive decline. Early Alzheimer's trials are underway. The brain has its own GLP-1 receptors — hinting that these drugs do far more neurologically than we first thought.

slides.heading: The Supply & Access Problem
slides.body: Demand outstripped supply for years, creating global shortages. At $900–$1,300/month without insurance in the US, access is deeply unequal. Biosimilars and oral pill versions entering the market by 2026 aim to change that equation.

slides.heading: Side Effects & Unknowns
slides.body: Nausea, vomiting, and muscle loss are common short-term concerns. Long-term effects beyond 5 years remain under study. Questions about what happens when people stop — and whether these are lifetime drugs — are still being answered.

slides.heading: A Drug Class for the Ages?
slides.body: GLP-1 drugs may be the most consequential pharmaceutical advance since statins. The challenge now is equitable access, understanding long-term safety, and ensuring medicine — not just markets — guides how these molecules change lives.
